scope: Actual logical direct/indirect consumers of the proposed supplier interfaces, plus nonlogical item-reference search. No native acceptance.
graph_method: Parsed all *fd*.md deps and justified_by supplier edges; initial five roots have empty aliases. Repository-wide rg over items and library for all five root IDs found no additional item-reference-only carrier outside this closure. Eight downstream items plus two root-as-consumer subjects are listed. No dependency edge changes are proposed.

reviews.review: Direct bounded-wall supplier use. The stated C1_t C2_x velocity and C_t C1_x pressure already have continuous classical restrictions; the theorem imposes homogeneous no-slip or stationary Navier slip itself. The energy integration and difference-energy uniqueness do not use an unspecified moving g. No equation, regularity hypothesis, force, beta, or uniqueness class changes.

Direct smooth-wall use and indirect uniqueness use. Its own g is C1([0,T];C2(Gamma;R3)), tangential, and explicitly typed, so it satisfies the proposed continuous wall-data convention. Its bounded C2 and periodic-channel branches, nonzero moving-wall work, stationary Navier dissipation, material-motion hypotheses, and conditional bounded-domain uniqueness all remain intact. No empirical applicability is inferred.

Direct bounded/exterior definition and indirect channel use. The remark says precisely that domain/regularity/trace/far-field conventions supply no existence theorem. Typing g and defining restrictions strengthens no existence conclusion and leaves every exterior/far-field limitation intact.

Direct channel use. The rapid-decay sine coefficients give jointly smooth time-first u on [0,infinity) times the closure, with zero classical traces. The periodic x,z geometry, heat synthesis, full smooth-flow difference-energy uniqueness and exponential decay are untouched; restricting to any finite interval fits the proposed evolution convention.

Direct channel use. Its polynomial steady velocity is continuous and C2 up to each wall, and g=0 is a continuous map on the two faces; its infinite-channel pressure is a separate space-only map with no added decay assumption. Periodic single-valued pressure obstruction and the shear-class uniqueness proof are unchanged.

Direct channel use; this is also a named proposal subject. The affine steady velocity and piecewise face-constant g are continuous on the disconnected wall boundary. The C2 competing shear class is retained because the proposed trace convention does not require C-infinity. Only F1 is repaired to call x streamwise and z transverse. Vorticity, flux, exact solution and shear-class uniqueness stay byte-identical.

Direct forced-model use; this is also a named proposal subject. The theorem explicitly adopts a distributional weak extension at its strong Sobolev regularity and expressly does not infer classical C2/C1 regularity. That alternative remains explicit, with H1_0 wall trace from V. The new conditional classical trace-extension requirement is not silently imposed on the weak extension. Reindexing u_phys(x,t)=u(t,x), likewise p,b, reconciles the physical supplier with existing space-first formulas without changing any numerical equation or bound.

Direct CFD consumer and indirect forced-model consumer. Its physical pressure functional already uses the space-first physical convention made explicit in the proposed theorem, so no formula needs editing. Its full Countable Choice, strong-solution, adopted weak extension, mean-zero gauge, initialization, actual-root and time-step hypotheses persist. xi remains mean zero with norm 1/sqrt(12); rho0 U0 ell0^4 and the qualified symbolic pressure bound remain correct.

Indirect smooth-wall consumer. Its affine/quadratic steady fields have smooth classical wall restrictions and the declared constant tangential g; explicit translation-equivariant shear material maps verify the mechanical-power supplier hypotheses. Both profiles, body force replacing periodic pressure drop, fluxes, vorticities and wall-power/dissipation identities remain sound conditional model predictions, with no measured-flow claim.

Indirect channel consumer. F=A sin(y/ell) has a smooth odd periodic extension, and the channel construction supplies the first sine mode before its periodic extension onto the torus. The exact constant-density compressible viscous substitution, pressure kappa rho_*^gamma, viscosity powers and absence of a general density-dependent existence claim are unchanged.
